rapids.name: Grave Creek Riffle
rapids.desc: An island split. Follow the main current down the tongue on the left. A boulder emerges below about 2,000 cfs.

rapids.name: Grave Creek Falls
rapids.desc: A ledge drop that can be run down the middle.

rapids.name: Sanderson Riffle
rapids.desc: A surf wave at some flows. A plaque on the cliff marks the 1964 flood.

rapids.name: Fish Ladder
rapids.desc: The standard run on the far right of Rainie Falls. There may be a queue; let boats clear the channel.

rapids.name: Middle Chute
rapids.desc: An alternative line, sometimes the only option for large rafts.

rapids.name: Rainie Falls
rapids.desc: The main drop: a 10 to 12 ft bedrock ledge with powerful reversals. Scout from river left; most boats take the Fish Ladder.

rapids.name: China Gulch Riffles
rapids.desc: Named for 1800s Chinese miners.

rapids.name: Big Slide Riffle
rapids.desc: The site of a late-1800s landslide.

rapids.name: Tyee Rapid
rapids.desc: A large house rock on the left. Work left to avoid the right wall; a gravel bar pushes the flow right.

rapids.name: Wildcat Rapid
rapids.desc: An island splits the flow; the right channel is usual. Willows and a wrap rock. Wrapping is reported at low flow.

rapids.name: Russian Rapid
rapids.desc: Long and splashy with several channels. Named for a legendary 1800s Russian miner.

rapids.name: Montgomery Chutes
rapids.desc: A defined tongue into wave trains. The left side is cleaner at low water.

rapids.name: Howard Creek Chutes
rapids.desc: Wave trains in a fast chute; take the left for the third wave train.

rapids.name: Slim Pickins Rapid
rapids.desc: A large split rock. Drift boats must use the narrow right channel; left is recommended for rafts.

rapids.name: Washboard Rapids
rapids.desc: A read-and-run wave train.

rapids.name: Plowshare Rapid
rapids.desc: Swirly. A pocket eddy on the left wall is a raft magnet.

rapids.name: Windy Creek Chutes
rapids.desc: Two chutes; oars may ship at low water.

rapids.name: Upper Black Bar Falls
rapids.desc: A steep drop into a large curling wave. Scout from river right and take the right line.

rapids.name: Lower Black Bar Falls
rapids.desc: A steep wave train. A rock on the left bank may cause a bump. Run the tongue right of center.

rapids.name: Little Windy Riffle
rapids.desc: Kayakers' "Eddy Alley", with small playful features below Black Bar Lodge.

rapids.name: Horseshoe Bend
rapids.desc: A tight right-left turn. Pass left of the bedrock island, then go right.

rapids.name: Telephone Hole
rapids.desc: Named for an old Forest Service telephone line. A ducky-flipping hole on the left.

rapids.name: Dulog Riffle
rapids.desc: Enter left and exit between the mid-river boulders. Scraping risk at low water.

rapids.name: Quiz Show
rapids.desc: A boulder garden. Move slowly.

rapids.name: Kelsey Creek Falls
rapids.desc: A left-side wave train.

rapids.name: Lower Kelsey
rapids.desc: Run center and pass right of any log at the entrance.

rapids.name: Battle Bar Riffle
rapids.desc: Stay right; a pillow rock midway.

rapids.name: Boulder Alley
rapids.desc: A boulder series; hidden rocks at lower water.

rapids.name: Big Boulder Rapids
rapids.desc: A fast chute right of Elephant Rock.

rapids.name: John's Rapid
rapids.desc: Named for Chief John (Tecumtum). Enter in the middle and pass right of the boulder.

rapids.name: China Bar Rapid
rapids.desc: Enter left. A "can opener" rock sits right of center; holes at low water.

rapids.name: Jaws
rapids.desc: Two tooth-like boulders on the left. Pass left of both and avoid the left hole.

rapids.name: Wall One
rapids.desc: Avoid the wall.

rapids.name: Telfer's Hole
rapids.desc: A ducky-flipping hole.

rapids.name: The Narrows
rapids.desc: The canyon tightens.

rapids.name: Coffee Pot
rapids.desc: The signature rapid of Mule Creek Canyon: bedrock constrictions create boils and surging eddy lines. Rated III by one guide and IV by American Whitewater.

rapids.name: Blossom Bar
rapids.desc: The hardest rapid of the trip. Boulders force the flow left into the "Picket Fence": enter left, then cut right above it. Scouting is advised for every boater. Boats wrapping and blocking the channel are common.

rapids.name: Devils Staircase Rapid
rapids.desc: A wave train just below Blossom Bar. Avoid the bottom-right wall and the helicopter eddy.

rapids.name: Quarter Inch Rapid
rapids.desc: Jet boats have about a quarter inch of clearance at low water. Read and run for rafts.

rapids.name: Solitude Rapid
rapids.desc: A "decision rock": pass left, since the right passage is now small.

rapids.name: Tacoma Rapids
rapids.desc: Enter right of center and exit left. Rocks on the right at low water.

rapids.name: Clay Hill Rapid
rapids.desc: The last significant rapid before Foster Bar. Stay right of the island and ride the inside of the turn. Rated II by one guide and III by American Whitewater.

rapids.name: Payton Riffle
rapids.desc: Exit right to avoid the left-side ledges.

rapids.name: Burnt Rapids
rapids.desc: The final Class II before the take-out.

rapids.name: Watson Riffle
rapids.desc: Most of the flow goes right around the island.

rapids.name: Foster Rapid
rapids.desc: The final riffle.

history: The western novelist Zane Grey owned the bar at Winkle Bar in the 1920s and built a cabin there in 1926.
Battle Bar is named for a fight in 1855-56 during the Rogue River Indian Wars.
Wild and Scenic designation in 1968 protected the Rogue from dams.

rules.d: A dedicated, reusable, washable, watertight system with a screw-on or latching gasket lid. Snap-on lids and RV toilets are not acceptable. Pouch systems (Biffy Bag, CleanWaste, ReStop2) are allowed with a watertight container for used pouches. Capacity is 1 pint per person per day.
Have the toilet out of the boat and accessible within 30 minutes of arriving at camp, away from the central camp area unless a pit toilet is on site. Urine may go in the river.
Untreated solid waste may be emptied only at the SCAT machine at Foster Bar or an RV dump station. The SCAT machine cannot take wipes, paper towels or trash.
A fire pan is required year-round for all campfires within 400 feet of the river. A shovel and a bucket of at least one gallon are required per party. Fireworks are prohibited.

A U.S. Coast Guard approved life jacket for each person, worn in Class III or greater rapids, and worn at all times by children 12 and younger on or near the water. Helmets are recommended in Class III and up.
Camping on the Wild section is first come, first served. Quiet hours are 10 p.m. to 6 a.m. Be prepared to share: large sites for 10 to 20 people are limited, so use one side if you are a small group.
Scavenged wood must be dead and down; cutting wood is prohibited. Fire restrictions change, so check with the Smullin Visitor Center. Gas and propane stoves are allowed.
Some pit toilets are being phased out. Prefer sites without one.
Remove all coolers, food, trash and waste from boats at night. Leaving attractants in boats teaches wildlife to claw and chew them.

From May 15 to October 15 the BLM maintains electric bear fences, food hoists and storage containers at some camps, including Whisky Creek, Horseshoe Bend, Rogue River Ranch, Half Moon Bar, Brushy Bar, Solitude, Tate Creek and Tacoma. Keep the fence turned on and closed at all times.
It is unlawful to habituate bears and other wildlife. Report sightings on the Bear Observation Form from permit check-in.
Scouting Blossom Bar is advised for all boaters. Passengers may walk around Rainie Falls, the Fish Ladder and Blossom Bar.
Extreme low flows can be as risky as high flows. Watch for trees, debris, landslides and wildfire on the shoreline.
Pass other groups in flatwater, not in rapids. Give fishing parties a wide berth.
Bring a leash for use on shore. Pet waste is handled like human waste and carried out in a watertight container.
The Bear Camp road is the fastest route but is closed November 5 to May 31 for snow and slides. Check road conditions first.

permit.status: Required year-round · lottery May 15 to Oct 15

items.d: For the control season (May 15 to October 15), apply on Recreation.gov from December 1 to January 31. Applications are online only. Results are emailed in mid-February with confirmation instructions.
Leftover dates are offered in a competitive phone call-in during the first five business days of April, 8 a.m. to 3 p.m., on 541-479-3735.

From May 5 to October 15, new permits are allocated by competitive call-in, 8 a.m. to 3 p.m., phone only. BLM posts open dates and space counts. Day-of-launch spaces go first come, first served or from a waiting list at the Smullin Visitor Center at Rand.
Control-season permits are picked up at the Smullin Visitor Center at Rand on launch day. Outside the control season you self-issue a permit at the Smullin Visitor Center or the Grave Creek drop box.
Party leaders must watch the Wild Rogue permit guidelines video once a year.
$6 non-refundable lottery application fee. $10 per person, paid when a reservation becomes a permit.
The river is regulated by the number of people launching each day, 120 in the control season, not by the number of groups.
Boat operators need Class IV skills. The Wild section has about three Class IV and nine Class III rapids.

Cancel the entire permit by 3 p.m. the day before launch. Email the Rogue River Permits office (preferred), or from May 5 to October 15 call 541-479-3735. Give the party leader, launch date and party size.
You can cancel individual spaces on a permit at any time without penalty. Non-confirmation or non-payment of a reservation also carries no penalty.
Failing to cancel an entire permit by the deadline puts the party leader on the no-show list: no permit for the rest of the year and all of the next year, including the lottery.
